policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'all the forms thereof' — plural noun with a third-person 'thereof' suffix, matching the qere צורתיו ('its forms'). The ketiv צורתי lacks the third-masculine suffix the ASV's 'thereof' renders.
ASV renders 'all the laws thereof' — plural, matching the qere תורתיו ('its laws'). The ketiv תורתו is singular 'its law', which the ASV plural does not reflect.

Qere והאריאל and ketiv והאראיל differ only in the order of two consonants and name the same word; the ASV's 'the altar hearth' renders either identically. No ASV note is mapped here, so nothing in the English distinguishes them and the qere base fallback carries the projection.

The ASV note on this verse reports the underlying Hebrew as 'fill the hands thereof' — plural 'hands', which is the qere ידיו. The ketiv ידו is singular 'his hand', so the translators' own literal gloss of the idiom they rendered 'consecrate it' shows the plural reading behind the text.
